newsitem.title: UK: Britain's new chancellor reforms Bank of England.
newsitem.headline: Britain's new chancellor reforms Bank of England.

text.p: Britain's new Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown on Tuesday announced substantial moves towards independence for the Bank of England.
The central bank now has "operational responsibility" for setting interest rates to meet an inflation target laid down by the Treasury.
The move stops short of full independence for the Bank and does not comply with the Maastricht criteria because the Treasury will still determine the inflation aim.
The new monetary framework will resemble that in New Zealand, a Treasury spokeswoman said.

The Treasury said the new Labour government had inherited the existing inflation target of 2.5 percent or less and this would be formally reconfirmed in Brown's Mansion House speech scheduled for June 12.
